notes: High-level: large distributed dev org building an IDE copilot platform for internal usage and OEM licensing to partners.
Primary ask: per-seat low-latency completions (streaming) with deterministic failover and model-version pinning per workspace.
Cost sensitivity: CFO wants clear per-seat unit economics; must show $/active-dev/month (target < $15/dev/month for baseline completions).
Engineering concerns: live streaming latency <= 100ms tail for common completions; cold-starts for new files tolerated up to 300ms.
Model preferences: preference for 7B/13B quantized variants for cost; legal requires no cross-customer data leakage; want private deployment behind VPC for pilot.
Quote (VP Eng): "If we can't predict cost per active seat, we can't roll this org-wide. Caching and good quantization profiles are must-haves."
POC scope: 300 simulated seats, three modes (IDE inline completion, multi-line refactor suggestions, code-search embeddings), collect latency/cost/quality metrics.

Cost experiments: running A/B on quantization (int8 vs int4 hybrid), batching policies, and prefix caching. Early result: int8 + KV caching = 28% unit-cost reduction, quality delta minimal on our eval prompts.
Routing needs: route pro-tier devs to lower-latency Dedicated pools, fall back to cost-optimized quantized variants under load. Want SLOs per route.
Integration notes: plugin will use streaming websocket with token-level attribution; requires trace headers for Redwood console observability.
Security notes: retention controls: 30/90/365 day options; they want 90-day by default for internal data, and audit logs retained 1 year. HSM for keys is a hard ask for procurement.
Internal stakeholders: VP Engineering (Eva Moreno), CTO (Liam Chen), Platform Lead (Rohit Iyer), Head of Security (Marta Silva).
Procurement path: POC -> security review -> pilot (Q3) -> org-wide rollout (Q4) if cost targets met.
Sales notes: emphasize Redwood Optimize recommendations (batching + quant profiles) and Dedicated autoscale to meet latency targets without overprovisioning.
Failure scenarios: if quantization leads to >4% regression on critical tests, they'll prefer larger model w/ caching; need automatic rollback policy in rollout configs.
Ask from AE/SE: provide detailed cost runbook (per-seat) + prebuilt eval prompts for code assistant quality regressions; sample SOW for Dedicated + Private deployment.
Links: see drive pricing deck + security FAQ (drive link), Fireflies of demo call, Gmail thread with legal, Jira for POC infra tickets.
